adds.title: Arkansas gender-marker rules: 1981 birth certificate law + DFA X descriptor policy
adds.summary: On February 19, 1981, Arkansas enacted Senate Bill 256, the Arkansas Vital Statistics Act of 1981, passed 34-0 in the Senate and 92-0 in the House, codifying authority to amend birth certificates to recognize surgical sex changes consistent with existing administrative practice, thereby creating a surgery-based pathway for trans people to conform Arkansas birth certificates to lived gender that remained in effect 40 years later.

adds.title: Intrastate Commerce Improvement Act (2015) and Arkansas Supreme Court Feb 2017 Fayetteville decision
adds.summary: Enacted February 24, 2015 as Act 137, Arkansas's Intrastate Commerce Improvement Act bars cities and counties from adopting or enforcing ordinances creating protected classifications or discrimination prohibitions not contained in state law, which does not include sexual orientation or gender identity, thereby preempting local trans-inclusive protections, as applied in February 2017 when the Arkansas Supreme Court invalidated Fayetteville's ordinance prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations.

adds.title: Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act - 2008 amendment and Kelly Loving Act (May 2025)
adds.summary: On May 16, 2025 Gov. Jared Polis signed House Bill 1312 — the Kelly Loving Act — passed May 6, 2025, which expands Colorado anti-discrimination protections in workplaces and schools to prohibit deadnaming and misgendering by requiring use of a person's chosen name and pronouns with immediate effect, requires schools with dress codes to allow choice from any uniform option with immediate effect, and simplifies changing gender identity on birth certificates and driver's licenses and changing names on marriage licenses effective October 1, 2026.
